## Description of the Problem

- Background: In modern Major League Baseball, front offices heavily rely on optical tracking data (Statcast) to evaluate and develop pitchers. Pitch design involved tweaking a pitcher's release point, velocity, and spin to alter the ball's movement profile.
- Motivation: Generating swings and misses (whiffs) is the most reliable way for a pitcher to record outs without relying on defensive fielding. Understanding the non-linear relationship between a pitch's physical characteristics and its ability to miss bats is highly valuable for both pre-game scouting and long-term player development.
- Question of Interest: What combination of velocity, spin rate, release extension, and induced movement maximizes the probability of generating a swing-and-miss on breaking balls (sliders, curveballs, sweepers, etc.)?
- Significance: Identifying the optimal physical profile for breaking balls allows teams to make targeted, data-driven recommendations to their pitching staff, enhancing overall staff strikeout rates.

## Description of the Data Set

- Source: MLB Statcast pitch-by-pitch data, accessed via the Python pybaseball library. The data is publicly avaliable and has been successfully downloaded and imported.
- Dimensions: Approximately 10,000 to 15,000 observations. The dataset will be filtered to only include breaking balls thrown by San Francisco Giants pitchers over the 2025 and 2026 seasons.
- Key Variables:
    - release_speed : Pitch velocity out of the hand (mph)
    - release_spin_rate : Spin rate of the pitch (rpm)
    - pfx_x : Horizontal movement in inches
    - pfx_z : Induced vertical break in inches
    - release_extension : How far off the mound the pitcher releases the ball (feet)
    - description : The outcome of the pitch, which will be changed into a target variable Whiff

## Supervised/Unsupervised. Regression/Classification

This is a supervised classification problem. The goal is to predict a bindary categorical response (Whiff vs No Whiff) based on labeled historical pitch data. The analysis will establish a baseline Logistic Regression model before exploring mroe flexible methods like QDA or KNN to capture non-linear movement boundaries.

## Commens/Concerns

One primary concern is class imblance. In baseball, whiffs occur on roughly 10-15% of all pitches. Because pitch accuracy alone is not an appropriate metric for heavily imbalanced classification, the models will be evaluated and tuned using alternite metrics such as PR-AUC or the F1-score to ensure the models are actually identifying whiffs rather than just predicting no-whiff.
